'''Sebastian A. "Subby" Anzaldo''' (August 3, 1933 – August 7, 2019)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.omaha.com/obits/anzaldo-sebastian-a-subby-sr/article_7f34afe4-e863-50ed-8c1f-1f1e2f410048.html|title=Anzaldo, Sebastian A. "Subby," Sr.|publisher=Omaha World Herald|accessdate=September 13, 2019}}</ref> was a booking agent, long-time City Council member, and [[List of mayors of Omaha|Mayor]] of [[Omaha, Nebraska]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/USAToday/access/55840003.html?dids=55840003:55840003&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jun+06%2C+1988&author=&pub=USA+TODAY+(pre-1997+Fulltext)&desc=NEBRASKA&pqatl=google | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604105831/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/USAToday/access/55840003.html?dids=55840003:55840003&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jun+06,+1988&author=&pub=USA+TODAY+(pre-1997+Fulltext)&desc=NEBRASKA&pqatl=google | url-status=dead | archive-date=June 4, 2011 | newspaper=USA Today | title=Nebraska | date=6 June 1988}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=DtkgAAAAIBAJ&sjid=IWsFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2514,4137874&dq=subby-anzaldo&hl=en |title=Omaha police want to bill for overtime |date=16 February 1993 |page=4 |newspaper=McCook Daily Gazette }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/orlandosentinel/access/77971325.html?dids=77971325:77971325&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Apr+28%2C+1994&author=&pub=Orlando+Sentinel&desc=OMAHA+MAYOR+SURPRISES+WITH+RESIGNATION+NEWS&pqatl=google |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604105756/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/orlandosentinel/access/77971325.html?dids=77971325:77971325&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Apr+28,+1994&author=&pub=Orlando+Sentinel&desc=OMAHA+MAYOR+SURPRISES+WITH+RESIGNATION+NEWS&pqatl=google |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 4, 2011 |title=Omaha mayor surprises with resignation news |date=28 April 1994 |newspaper=Orlando Sentinel }}</ref>

== Career ==
Anzaldo worked as a saxophone player in the Omaha area before expanding into construction contracting and then later as a theatrical booking agent.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/USAToday/access/55840003.html?dids=55840003:55840003&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jun+06%2C+1988&author=&pub=USA+TODAY+%28pre-1997+Fulltext%29&desc=NEBRASKA&pqatl=google |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120720140118/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/USAToday/access/55840003.html?dids=55840003:55840003&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jun+06,+1988&author=&pub=USA+TODAY+(pre-1997+Fulltext)&desc=NEBRASKA&pqatl=google |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 20, 2012 |title=Nebraska |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |date=6 June 1988 }}</ref><ref name=Gonzalez>{{cite news |last1=Cindy |first1= Gonzalez |title= Anzaldo Moves into the Spotlight on City Council|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/omaha-world-herald/145758570/ |newspaper=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=May 27, 1988 |pages=[https://www.newspapers.com/article/omaha-world-herald/145758570/ 1], [https://www.newspapers.com/article/omaha-world-herald/145758813/ 8] |accessdate= |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He had been active in Omaha politics having served on the Zoning Board of Appeals, the Charter Review Committee, the Parks and Recreation Advisory Board, the City Planning Board, and the Police Advisory Committee.<ref name=Gonzalez/> On May 26, 1988, he was named to the [[Omaha City Council]] for district 3<ref name=Gonzalez/> after Walter Calinger vacated his seat to serve as mayor after the death of mayor Bernie Smith.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1=  |title=Anzaldo Elected to Omaha council |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/lincoln-journal-star/145760187/ |newspaper=[[Lincoln Journal Star]] |date=May 27, 1988 |pages=|accessdate= |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Anzaldo was sworn in on June 6, 1988.<ref name=Gonzalez/>

Anzaldo served as acting mayor, following the resignation of his predecessor [[P.J. Morgan]], from September 20, 1994<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/chicagotribune/access/24156902.html?dids=24156902:24156902&FMT=CITE&FMTS=CITE:FT&type=current&date=Apr+27%2C+1994&author=&pub=Chicago+Tribune+%28pre-1997+Fulltext%29&desc=SURPRISE!+OMAHA+MAYOR+RESIGNS&pqatl=google |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604105816/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/chicagotribune/access/24156902.html?dids=24156902:24156902&FMT=CITE&FMTS=CITE:FT&type=current&date=Apr+27,+1994&author=&pub=Chicago+Tribune+(pre-1997+Fulltext)&desc=SURPRISE!+OMAHA+MAYOR+RESIGNS&pqatl=google |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 4, 2011 |title=Surprise! Omaha mayor resigns |date=27 April 1994 |newspaper=Chicago Tribune }}</ref> to January 9, 1995.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Daub wins Omaha mayor race |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=ttsgAAAAIBAJ&sjid=D2sFAAAAIBAJ&pg=4044,5590258&dq=hal-daub+omaha&hl=en |newspaper=McCook Daily Gazette |date=13 December 1994 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.omahapubliclibrary.org/subjects/society/history/mayors.html |publisher=Omaha Public Library |title=Mayors of Omaha |access-date=11 February 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090512054719/http://www.omahapubliclibrary.org/subjects/society/history/mayors.html |archive-date=12 May 2009 }}</ref>

In 2019, he was inducted into the Nebraska Music Hall of Fame.<ref>{{cite web |last1= |first1=  |title= Subby Anzaldo memorial |url=https://www.omahaitaly.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/September-2019-Newsletter.pdf |website=The Italian American Heritage Society of Omaha|date=September 11, 2019 |pages=6|accessdate= |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>
